origins.Brazil: The week was defined by extreme volatility and shifting liquidity. Earlier in the week, the strong KC rally allowed buyers to meet sellers' asking prices, improving flow and creating attractive coverage opportunities. As prices moved higher, sellers became increasingly defensive, reducing available liquidity both domestically and on the FOB side. By the end of the week, the sharp correction led buyers to lower their bids aggressively, while sellers showed little willingness to adjust, widening the bid-offer gap and leaving the market largely locked once again. As a general sentiment, and despite the volatility, exporters are being able to cover their shorts. The Rio Minas market also showed a lot of volatility. Reported traded volume, however, remained moderate. Conillon differentials remained practically unchanged on a week- on-week basis. Overall availability remains good, but recent price increases scared off sellers.
origins.Colombia: No changes from last week. Due to the high market volatility, over the weekend, intermediaries preferred to wait to sell their inventory during the week, expecting the market to continue rising and find better prices. Due to the El Niño phenomenon, the government is taking preventive measures to avoid potential disruptions to the power supply caused by the decrease in the initial water levels of rivers and reservoirs. The main risk for the 26/27 main crop is quality defects due to underfilling and broca. For the 26/27 Mitaca, the risk is in coffee volume, since the flowering could be affected by high temperatures. External demand remains low due to high prices for Q4.
origins.Peru: Origin remains highly unsettled, and the ongoing volatility continues to weigh on market activity. Elevated price levels, combined with the uncertainty, are limiting liquidity, with flow still well below what the market had anticipated, pending a lower crop this year. CAM / MEXICO The situation is similar across Central America/Mexico. Market participants remain cautious amid the current volatility, which many view as disconnected from the underlying fundamentals. There is growing discussion around the rationale for offering lower differentials when Colombia and Peru remain expensive, as Centrals are expected to become an important replacement origin. At the same time, there is concern about the impact of the upcoming Brazilian crop on market direction. Overall, suppliers remain open to discussing differentials but are primarily focused on analyzing bids rather than committing to new business. As a result, feedback from origin remains slow, with activity continuing at a cautious pace.
origins.Tanzania: Robusta dry cherry auctions are running on a weekly basis, with green coffee already flowing to the market. Port operations in Dar es Salaam remain smooth and efficient, with no disruptions to export logistics at this time.
origins.Uganda: The recent London rally supported stronger local prices, encouraging producers to sell and improving availability for nearby execution. origins.Indonesia: The KC rally incentivized a few buyers to take the opportunity to lock in lower diffs on forward shipments. origins.Brazil: Fine cup volumes are expected to increase from mid-July, with larger screen sizes maintaining a 25% share in incoming lots and price per bag rising, presenting sourcing opportunities if liquidity arrives before New York selling off. Near-term demand for July is minimal, with most buyers seeking coffee for August to December deliveries, and last-minute buyers are trying to capitalize on differentials. It seems local roasters in Brazil are struggling to secure enough coffee for July deliveries due to rising prices and are waiting for better buying opportunities. Sellers are only committing to quick deliveries, making it difficult to secure forward contracts for August, despite active trading in the past week. If this activity was to last it could cause potential operational bottlenecks which is something to keep in mind for exporters and buyers.
origins.Colombia: With the coffee year harvest at 71% and the Mitaca crop 56% completed, the Colombian internal market is becoming very tight. The main coffee export figure for 25/26 was reduced to 12.4 million bags (Sucafina's figure). According to the FNC, production was higher than in May 25, but exports were lower due to a delayed mitaca and high Colombian prices discouraging external demand. Meanwhile, imports have increased +198.6% year to date, reaching 775k bags as of April 25 .
origins.Peru: The Peruvian harvest is at its peak. Differentials are remaining firm and offers for September are scarce, making it difficult to take positions for most exporters, resulting in slow market activity. However, the new crop in Central America and Mexico presents some opportunities.
origins.Tanzania: The 2026/27 crop season is now underway across Tanzania. Robusta dry cherry auctions are running on a weekly basis, with green coffee expected to begin flowing to the market within the next one to two weeks. On the Arabica side, mills are set to officially open their doors to cooperative deliveries from next week, marking the formal start of the Arabica intake season. Early crop indications are encouraging; production is forecast at 3–5% above last season's volumes for both Arabica and Robusta, mainly supported by a combination of an on-cycle crop and first harvests from newly established plantations. origins.Brazil: Throughout the week, the Arabica market remained tight with low volumes hitting the market despite New York volatility and the USD strengthening. Liquidity improved mid-week, not due to increased selling pressure but because exporters were able to match sellers’ asking prices during the NY rally. As Ny became more volatile and eventually softened, market activity slowed down, with buyers stepping back and bid/offers spread widening again. Main trading activity is mostly concentrated on GC, especially new crop and Zona da Mata lots, while FC remained tighter and more selective due to ongoing quality issues linked to rains, resulting in firmer differentials, especially for higher screens. On the Conilon side, the market remained well offered during the week, with a good volume of trades reported. Prices in BRL have improved following the recent rallies, and differentials have remained stable overall. Sellers continued to try to push the prices higher in order to improve the average selling price. Exporters and local merchants were active, covering nearby shorts, while local roasters were not participating as the prices shot higher.
origins.Colombia: The domestic market showed a notable improvement in coffee flow during the week, as producers released a larger share of previously withheld stocks, leading to increased commercialization across producing regions. Despite this, competition for available coffee remains intense, with exporters and local buyers actively securing volume, keeping differentials elevated. Demand continues to be particularly strong for 2027 coverage, with buyers maintaining solid interest in Colombian coffee despite higher replacement costs and, in some cases, exploring alternative origins.
origins.Peru: In the north, market conditions continue to support very strong local prices, with availability from cooperatives and key suppliers remaining tight. Ongoing volatility has also limited producers’ willingness to commit to forward sales, pushing sourcing costs higher as buyers must compete with prevailing parchment market prices. In the central region, larger exporters have remained intermittent in their participation, entering the market to cover short-term needs before withdrawing in anticipation of potential price corrections. However, despite the recent futures rally, local prices have held firm and continue to show underlying strength. RWANDA & BURUNDI Harvest is estimated to be 96% and 95% completed, respectively, in Burundi the crop was good and in line with exporters’ projections. In Rwanda, the season will conclude in the next 2-3 weeks in all regions and we estimate the crop to be 35% smaller than last year’s.
origins.Uganda: Slight improvement in coffee flow was observed following the market uptick and improved drier weather conditions in the field. Competition remains tight but less aggressive, as earlier June/July commitments made in anticipation of peak harvest continue to weigh on near-term demand. The macro environment is relatively stable, with FX moving lower week-on-week, while fuel prices remain elevated despite expectations of easing in line with broader global trends. Weather conditions are more favorable, with reduced rainfall supporting ripening, drying, and ongoing harvest activity. On the Arabica side, exporters are remaining short and delays must be expected. New York bearish trend resulted in firming up the differentials despite the recent rally, slowing down the purchase activities. Farmers and local traders are holding up the little volume they have and it seems no one is really buying at the prices they are asking.
origins.Vietnam: Overall, the competition has been very stiff in the Robusta market. Producers sold during the London rally as the prices got pushed up. Seasonal rains persisted across key regions and the currency remained stable. origins.Brazil: Compared to last week, the market clearly shifted from a downside acceleration to a tentative stabilization, although liquidity remains very limited. Last week ended with a sharp correction, driven by weaker futures and increased new crop pressure. This week, price action turned more sideways with a slightly firmer tone, primarily supported by short-covering activity from exporters. However, overall traded volumes are remaining below average, and the lack of strong participation in the market is still concerning. The Rio Minas market remains tight with firms’ differentials, even with the recent NY rally. Buyers are holding off purchases while sellers are pushing for sales in this new market structure, as the new crop offers are starting to show up. On the Conilon front, the week turned out to be quite an active one, with some good volume traded following the LND rally. Sellers participated more as the harvest progressed, scaling up the prices and improving the overall average selling price. Buyers are continuing to cover their nearby shorts on an opportunistic basis and are trying to do so before the big rally by trying to maintain stable differentials as long as possible.
origins.Colombia: Colombia’s in the latter part of the first half of Mitaca. Coffee availability got better last weekend, but prices remain elevated and very firm. Retention is being seen for higher prices. An appreciating COP in the run-up to the election is making things harder on the FOB differential. All eyes will be on this Sunday’s presidential election results and their FX impacts. RWANDA & BURUNDI Harvest is estimated to be 94% and 85% completed, respectively. The competition has started to draw down due to the New York correction. Most of the harvest is expected to be completed by the end of June and mid-July, respectively. At the moment, both origins are putting the focus on the production of their Specialty batches.
origins.Uganda: The Robusta crop is under close look. Timely monitoring is of the essence as the harvest has been largely delayed; the crop is estimated to be 45% harvested and about 20% commercialized. The competition in the field is intense as most exporters are short on nearby shipments. Arabica parchment season is supposed to be in full swing, but the New York bearish trend and volumes being at a record low resulted in a standstill from a business point of view. Local traders are not willing to adjust the cash price as they bought expensive coffee. Most exporters have now covered their shorts, meaning traders will have to capitulate at some point. North West parchment season is expected to peak in about 1 month; this might unlock the situation, depending on the volume that region is generating.
origins.Indonesia: The Robusta crop is estimated to be 47% harvested and 33% commercialized. The flow of arrivals remained stable in Lampung during the week. 25% of the market is dominated by mostly 1 exporter. Price structure in the field has not changed much; differentials are remaining firm despite the London rally at the end of the week.
origins.Vietnam: London continued to edge up slightly, therefore slowing down the activity on the local market and reducing the selling pressure. origins.Brazil: The Arabica market shifted from early resistance to a sharp late-week correction and now sits in a phase of low-liquidity consolidation. Overall, the market is in a post-correction price discovery, the Rio Minas market remains very tight and prices are still firm. The first lots from Rio Minas are starting to be seen, but volumes are remaining tight. On the Robusta side, as the harvest progresses, the volumes of offers are improving, but not sufficiently to cover a growing nearby demand. Replacement differentials have softened a little, thanks to the national holiday, resulting in many buyers being out of the market and forcing sellers to lower their prices to find business.
origins.Colombia: Colombia experienced a quiet week in terms of trading activity following the first round of elections. Some key players are continuing to dominate the market by offering high prices, causing intermediaries and smaller exporters to delay sales or exit the market, despite slow payments and intakes.
origins.Peru: The crop is expected to contract by 7% compared to last year. These estimates are resulting in suppliers exercising increased caution with respect to position-taking and overall risk appetite. Harvest progress is currently at approximately 32%, with the peak period expected during the second half of June through the first half of July. From a market perspective, conditions remain largely unchanged. Market volatility has not been significant enough to justify any improvements to differentials and suppliers remain primarily focused on short covering, a trend that is expected to continue over the coming weeks. Therefore, differentials remain firm, reflecting the factors noted above. CENTRALS & MEXICO Overall, weather conditions have been positive to date, particularly during March and April, which are critical months for flowering development. While May concluded with below-average rainfall levels, conditions were not excessively dry, and healthy soil moisture levels have thus far been sufficient to support crop development. Looking ahead, it will be necessary to closely monitor any potential impact from El Niño-related weather patterns, particularly the risk of drier-than-normal conditions affecting cherry filling development. Suppliers remain motivated and are continuing to improve agricultural practices, supported by the strong price incentives observed during the current crop season.
origins.Tanzania: The 2026/27 season is approaching. Cherry development and ripening across both Arabica and Robusta growing regions is progressing well, with early indicators pointing to stronger production versus the prior season. The combination of an on-cycle crop and the first harvests from newly established plantations is expected to drive a 3–5% increase in volume. Across the supply chain, stakeholders are mobilizing ahead of the new season, with cherry picking already underway in select areas. Port operations continue to run smoothly. RWANDA & BURUNDI Harvest is estimated to be 90% and 78% completed, respectively; the competition has started to draw down due to the New York correction. Last week's rains will help the remaining cherries ripen. Most of the harvest is expected to be completed by the end of June and mid-July, respectively. The crop will be about 35% smaller than last year's overall.
origins.Uganda: The general crop flow is slower than expected and slower than the last two main crops. With the market on a downward trend last week, local traders are still hesitant to sell at prevailing market prices. Current weather trends are not significantly affecting production but causing delays in crop maturation, drying and harvesting. Arabica parchment season is supposed to be in full swing, but the New York bearish trend and volumes being at a record low resulted in a standstill from a business point of view. Local traders are not willing to adjust the cash price as they buy expensive coffee. Most exporters have now covered their shorts, meaning traders will have to capitulate at some point. Northwest parchment season is expected to peak in about 1 month; this might unlock the situation, depending on the volume that region is generating. The Ebola outbreak is still being contained by the WHO and the Ministry of Health SOPs and preventive measures. At the moment, there is no notable impact on crop flow and coffee movement.
origins.Indonesia: Peak season has started. Arrivals rose by 30% from the previous week. Competition is stiff, with a couple of exporters being very aggressive. Overall, it is a tough year and local exporters are being the most exposed to this intense competition.
origins.Vietnam: Farmers are conducting the 1st round of fertilizers. Though fertilizer prices have increased by 20-30% this year, farmers are still planning to keep the same level of input. origins.Peru: Peru's crop flow is accelerating, with over 25% sold. Firm differentials are expected to persist until shorts are covered by exporters and the arbitrage with Colombia narrows down.

origins.Colombia: Colombia’s Mitaca harvest is underway following expected seasonal patterns, with strong cherry development supported by favorable weather conditions. While volumes are projected to be slightly lower than last year, quality remains a key highlight. Harvesting is expected to begin mid-April in the region, with lower altitude farms peaking first (May-June) and high altitude farms following in June-July.
origins.Burundi: The season is at 80% harvested, it is expected to wrap up in June. Differentially, coffee is still expensive and completely disconnected from KC.
origins.Rwanda: The season is 55% harvested, in the middle of the peak. Weather conditions are favorable and quality seems to be promising. Volumes are increasing. The government has announced it will maintain last year's cherry price even though KC has corrected.
origins.Tanzania: In Tanzania, the 2026/27 crop is progressing well. Cherry development across both Arabica and Robusta regions is encouraging, with early indications suggesting a higher production compared to the previous season. Government agencies and coffee regulators are getting ready to begin the new season in the coming weeks. Port performance remains stable and steady.
origins.Uganda: The Robusta new crop flow has picked up. Most exporters are still covering May and June shipments, firming up differentials for the time being. Regular rains have delayed ripening and drying. We still expect a broadly unchanged crop on year, but it’s a clear delay. For the Arabica, the crop is ending and was 60%-70% smaller than last year. Differentials on Parchment and Drugar are still expensive even though KC corrected.

origins.Brazil: The Brazilian Arabica market remains tight with low liquidity. On the producer side, we are still seeing a lot of retention due to the price gap between late harvest and new crop. Producers remain well capitalized and it is expected that they will start releasing coffee as the harvest moves on. The environment remains misaligned in price expectations, which has constrained the closing of several substantial businesses. origins.Guatemala: Guatemala's president declared a state of siege on Sunday after security forces freed dozens of prison guards held hostage by inmates, ending a weekend of gang violence that left at least seven police officers dead and another 10 injured. Rioting inmates had taken 46 hostages at three men's prisons early on Saturday. Gang-led violence targeted police in several areas around Guatemala City after security forces regained control of the prison. President Bernardo Arevalo declared a 30-day state of siege that he said would allow the full force of the state, including the police and the army, to combat gang violence. Under Guatemalan law, a state of siege can temporarily limit or suspend civil liberties and expand security forces' powers in response to threats to public order. Earlier on Sunday, National Civil Police director David Boteo had advised Guatemalans to stay at home, and the U.S. Embassy in Guatemala issued a security warning for U.S. citizens. Guatemala's education minister canceled school classes across the country, which Arevalo said was a preventive measure.
origins.Brazil: Local prices have been gradually easing over the past few weeks, prompting growers and local traders to back off from the marketplace. origins.Colombia: Days after US President Trump threatened Colombia with a similar intervention to Venezuela’s, a phone call between the countries’ leaders took place, defusing the situation. UNITED STATES The U.S. military conducted a major operation in Venezuela, capturing President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, in a raid on January 3, 2026. This involved air and ground forces targeting military infrastructure and Maduro’s compound, leading to clashes, casualties and a declaration of general mobilization by Venezuela, followed by global outcry over the legality of the action. origins.Indonesia: As we reported last week, torrential rains of unprecedented scale inundated the Sumatra provinces of Aceh, North Sumatra, and West Sumatra due to Cyclone Senyar. Widespread flooding and landslides have severed road access, electricity, and communication.
